comments.en: One who was reading the Shema and made a mistake, and skipped in it one verse, [he] should not begin to read that verse by itself, but rather should go back to that verse and complete [the Shema, from that point on] until the end. And the same [applies] to Hallel, to prayer [of Shemoneh Esreh], and to the Megillah [of Esther]. One who entered a synagogue and found that [the congregation] has read half of it (i.e. the Shema) and [he] completed [the remaining half of the Shema] with them, [he] should not go back and read it (i.e. the Shema) from the beginning until that place, but rather [he] should begin from the beginning and complete it until the end. And the same [applies] to Hallel, to Tefillah (prayer) [of Shemoneh Esreh], and to the Megillah [of Esther].
comments.he: הקורא את שמע וטעה והשמיט בה פסוק אחד לא יחזור ויקרא את הפסוק בפני עצמו אלא מתחיל באותו פסוק וגומר עד סוף וכן בהלל וכן במגלה וכן בתפלה. הנכנס לבית הכנסת ומצאן שקראו חצייה וגמר עמהן לא יחזור ויקרא מראשה עד אותו מקום אלא מתחיל מראש וגומר עד סוף וכן בהלל וכן בתפלה וכן במגלה.

comments.en: We do not say anything [personal] after [the Beracha (blessing) of] Emet Veyatziv. But we do say [personal] things after [the] prayer [of Shmoneh Esreh], even if it is [as long as] the confession (Vidui) of Yom Kippur.
comments.he: אין אומרין ד"א אמת ויציב אבל אומרין ד"א תפלה אפילו כסדר וידוי יוה"כ.

comments.en: If, along the road, you chance upon a bird’s nest, in any tree or on the ground, with fledglings or eggs and the mother sitting over the fledglings or on the eggs, do not take the mother together with her young.
comments.he: כִּ֣י יִקָּרֵ֣א קַן־צִפּ֣וֹר ׀ לְפָנֶ֡יךָ בַּדֶּ֜רֶךְ בְּכׇל־עֵ֣ץ ׀ א֣וֹ עַל־הָאָ֗רֶץ אֶפְרֹחִים֙ א֣וֹ בֵיצִ֔ים וְהָאֵ֤ם רֹבֶ֙צֶת֙ עַל־הָֽאֶפְרֹחִ֔ים א֖וֹ עַל־הַבֵּיצִ֑ים לֹא־תִקַּ֥ח הָאֵ֖ם עַל־הַבָּנִֽים׃

comments.en: If you see your fellow’s ox or sheep gone astray, do not ignore it; you must take it back to your fellow.
comments.he: לֹֽא־תִרְאֶה֩ אֶת־שׁ֨וֹר אָחִ֜יךָ א֤וֹ אֶת־שֵׂיוֹ֙ נִדָּחִ֔ים וְהִתְעַלַּמְתָּ֖ מֵהֶ֑ם הָשֵׁ֥ב תְּשִׁיבֵ֖ם לְאָחִֽיךָ׃

sections.en: Concluding the laws of prayer in this tractate, the mishna raises several prayer-related matters. This mishna speaks of certain innovations in the prayer formula that warrant the silencing of a communal prayer leader who attempts to introduce them in his prayers, as their content tends toward heresy. One who recites in his supplication: Just as Your mercy is extended to a bird’s nest, as You have commanded us to send away the mother before taking her chicks or eggs (Deuteronomy 22:6–7), so too extend Your mercy to us; and one who recites: May Your name be mentioned with the good or one who recites: We give thanks, we give thanks twice, they silence him. This mishna and the next one deal with the communal prayer leader. (If one says: “May the good bless You,” this is a path of heresy.) One who is passing before the ark, as prayer leader, and erred, another should immediately pass in his place, and at that moment, this replacement should not refuse in the interest of courtesy. The Amida prayer was interrupted and he should replace him as quickly as possible. From where does the replacement commence? From the beginning of the blessing in which the former had erred.
sections.he: הָאוֹמֵר עַל קַן צִפּוֹר יַגִּיעוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ, וְעַל טוֹב יִזָּכֵר שְׁמֶךָ, מוֹדִים מוֹדִים, מְשַׁתְּקִין אוֹתוֹ. הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה וְטָעָה, יַעֲבֹר אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו, וְלֹא יְהֵא סָרְבָן בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה. מִנַּיִן הוּא מַתְחִיל, מִתְּחִלַּת הַבְּרָכָה שֶׁטָּעָה בָהּ:

en: הַבְטָחָה f. (בָּטַח) assurance, divine promise, faith. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 38 באתה הה׳ the promise came true. Berakhot 17ᵃ גדולה ה׳ וכ׳ the divine promise (of reward) to women is greater &c. Ib. V, 4; Sotah 38ᵇ ואם הַבְטָחָתוֹ וכ׳ but if he is confident that &c. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 76 אין ה׳ לצדיקים וכ׳ the rigtheous do not rely on the divine promise in this world (they are afraid, lest their sin may have caused its withdrawal, see Berakhot 4ᵇ). Mekhilta Yithro section (Parashah) 2 אנשי אמת אלו בעלי ה׳ (Variant אַבְטָחָה) ‘men of truth’ (Shemot XVIII, 21) that means men having faith in God; and e.—plural הַבְטָחוֹת. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 19 הרי כל ה׳ וכ׳ are these all the promises held out to the proselyte &c.?; and from

טֵירוּף, טֵרוּף m. (טָרַף)
1) (subaudi הדעת) confusion, distraction; trouble. Berakhot V, 4 (34ᵃ) מפני הטי׳ because he might become confused (and be unable to resume his prayers); Devarim Rabbah section (Parashah) 7, beginning—Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VIII, 13 בט׳ הדעת in confusion (not in concert).—Midrash Tanḥuma Mick. 2 נטרף טרוף אחד had only one trouble (about the interpretation of his dream).—plural טֵירוּפִין, טֵר׳. Ib. נטרף שני ט׳ had two troubles (not knowing even the dream).—Sifré Devarim 296 (reference. to בדרך, Devarim XXV, 17) בשעת טֵיוּפֵיכֶם when you were in a state of disorder.

—2) ejection, banishment (compare טֵירוּדִין). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 15; Midrash Till. to Psalms CXXXIX (omitt. in ed. Bub.); Yalkut ib. 887 טֵירוּפִי מתוכה my banishment from Eden.

כַּף common gender. (Biblical Hebrew; [something arched, hollow,]
1) palm of the hand, hand.—Dual כַּפַּיִם. Yerushalmi Berakhot I, 3ᶜ bottom of page, see חָטַף. Nazir 46ᵇ, see כָּנָף; and from—נשא כ׳ to raise the hands, to pronounce the priestly benediction. Berakhot V, 4 לא ישא את כַּפָּיו must not pronounce &c.; and from

—2) sole of the foot. Du. as ab. Chullin 70ᵇ מהלכי כ׳ animals walking on soles (having no split hoofs, Vayikra XI, 27).—Transferred glove; sole of the shoe. Kelim XXVI, 3 כף לוקטי(ם) קוצים (Rabbenu Shimshon כפלוקטי) the thorn-pickers’ glove. Tosefta Kelim Bava Batra IV, 5 רוב כף אחת, the larger portion of one sole; כל כף אחת the whole of &c.

—3) the crest (fleshy elevation) over the genitals. Tosefta Niddah VI, 4, sq. עד שתפשט את הכף (Variant משתתפשט) when the crest (of the girl) begins to flatten; Yerushalmi Yevamot I, 2ᵈ bottom of page עד שתתפשט הכף; Yerushalmi Sanhedrin VIII, beginning 26ᵃ משתתפשט הכ׳ (of a male); Niddah 47ᵃ, sq. נתמעך הכ׳ the crest grows lower. Ib. 52ᵇ אחת על הכ׳ one hair on the crest; and e.

—4) pan, censer. Tamid V, 4 (containing the בָּזָךְ). Ib. VII, 2 כף וכסויה the censer and its lid; and from—plural כַּפּוֹת. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 14; and e.

—5) spoon, mason’s trowel &c. Kelim XIII, 2; 4; and from Shabbat VIII, 5 כ׳ סיד, explained ib. 80ᵇ כ׳ של סיידין the plasterers’ trowel.—plural כַּפִּים, כַּפִּין. Middot III, 4 כפין של ברזל Arukh (ed. כפיס, Variant כפים) iron trowels.

—6) (with, or without מאזנים) scale of the balance. Pirkei Avot II, 8. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Aḥăré, p. 167ᵃ כ׳ עוונות וכ׳ the scale of sins on the one side, and that of merits on the other; והקב"ה מטה לכ׳ זכות and the Lord bends (the balance) towards the scale of merits. Pirkei Avot I, 6, see זְכוּת; and from—Du. כַּפַּיִים, כַּפַּיִין. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia II, 5 (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) כיפין, read: כפיין).

—7) shore, banks (see כֵּיפָא). Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 13, see חָף.—plural כַּפִּים, constr. כַּפֵּי. Eicha Rabbah introduction (R. Ḥăn. 3) (transl. גיא המלח, II Chr. XXV, 11) כ׳ המלח the salt shores.

שָׁם (Biblical Hebrew) there, thither. Makkot II, 7 אינו יוצא מִשָּׁם לעולם he dare not go away from there (the city of refuge) all his life time; שם תהא דירתו שם וכ׳ there he must live, there he must die &c.; Tosefta ib. III (II), 5. Makkot 4ᵃ שנפל שם which fell thereinto. Berakhot V, 4 אם אין שם כהן וכ׳ if no priest besides him is present; and see from—Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VIII, 9 שָׁמָּה, see רגָּז.—לְשָׁם thither. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 18; and from

תֵּבָה, תֵּיבָה (Biblical Hebrew תֵּבָה; Egyptian; see, however, תָּבָא)
1) ship, ark, chest. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 31 (play on קנים, Breishit VI, 14) מה הקן … אף תֵּיבָתְךָ וכ׳ as birds (see קֵן) make the leper clean, so does thy ark cleanse thee. Ib. על שם תֵּיבָתוֹ של נח (it is called t’biḳin) from the measures of Noah’s ark. Yerushalmi Eruvin V, 22ᶜ bottom of page כיצד היו ישראל … כת׳ how did the Israelites march in the desert?… like a chest (forming a square), opposed כקורה like a beam (in columns). Menachot 94ᵇ כמין ת׳ פרוצה (the shape of the show-bread was) that of an open chest (without a lid and with a level bottom), opposed כמין ספינה רוקדת like a rocking ship (with a curved bottom). Sifra M’tsorʿa, Zavim, Parah 1, Chaldaic II תֵּיבַת הבלנים the bathers’ chest. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia X, 1, sq.; and from—plural תֵּבוֹת, תֵּי׳. Midrash Till. to Psalms I היה צריך לעשות ת׳ הרבה he would have been obliged to build many arks. Yerushalmi Sotah VIII, beginning 22ᵇ שהיו עשויין ת׳ ת׳ they (the Egyptians) were arrayed in squares.—Esp. the chest in the synagogue containing the scrolls of the Pentateuch. Sotah 38ᵇ, see פְּסַק. Taanit II, 1 מוציאין את הת׳ וכ׳ (at prayer meetings) they bring the chest out to the open place of the town, and put ashes of wood on the chest &c. Megillah III, 1 בני העיר … בה"כ לוקחין ת׳ ת׳ וכ׳ if the citizens of a township sell … a synagogue, they may buy (for the money) a book chest; if they sell a chest, they may buy book wrappers; and from—עבר לפני הת׳, ירד לפני הת׳ to go before the chest, to act as reader of prayers. Berakhot 34ᵃ שירד לפני הת׳ וכ׳ who recited the prayers in the presence of &c. Ib. V, 3 העובר לפני הת׳ וטעה וכ׳ if a reader makes a mistake (reads heretical formulas), another person must pass before the chest in his place. Ib. 4. Ib. 34ᵃ העובר לפני הת׳ צריך לסרב he that is asked to read the prayers &c., see סָרַב. Taanit II, 2 מורידין לפני הת׳ וכ׳ we depute as reader (on fast days) an old man &c.; and see from

—2) word. Menachot 30ᵇ ת׳ בת שתי וכ׳ a word of two letters. Shabbat 104ᵃ they did not know הי באמצע ת׳ וכ׳ in which (of the two forms of the letters מנצפ"ך) were to be employed in the middle of a word, and which at the end; and from—plural תֵּיבוֹת, תֵּיבִיּוֹת. Chullin 64ᵇ דפסק … ת׳ (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 40) where the scribe divides them into two words; ib. 65ᵃ. Yerushalmi Megillah I, 71ᶜ bottom of page תיביות; and e.

comments.en: [A person] who prays [Shmoneh Esreh] must pay attention [to the meaning of the words]. Abba Shaul says, “There is a reference for [the need of attention in] prayer [in the Tanach], ‘Prepare their hearts, pay attention.’ “ (Psalms 10:17)
comments.he: המתפלל צריך שיכוין את לבו אבא שאול אומר סימן לדבר (תהילים י) תכין לבם תקשיב אזנך.

sections.en: In order to prevent the prayer leader from erring in his prayer, it was said that one who passes before the ark should not respond amen after the blessing of the priests, because of potential confusion. Since the mishna is describing a situation in which he was praying without a prayer book, responding amen would interrupt the order of the prayer and potentially lead him to begin a different blessing. For this reason, even if there is no priest other than the communal prayer leader, he does not lift his hands to bless the people, lest he become confused. And, however, if he is certain that he can lift his hands and resume his prayer without becoming confused, he is permitted to recite the blessing.
sections.he: הָעוֹבֵר לִפְנֵי הַתֵּיבָה, לֹא יַעֲנֶה אַחַר הַכֹּהֲנִים אָמֵן, מִפְּנֵי הַטֵּרוּף. וְאִם אֵין שָׁם כֹּהֵן אֶלָּא הוּא, לֹא יִשָּׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו. וְאִם הַבְטָחָתוֹ שֶׁהוּא נוֹשֵׂא אֶת כַּפָּיו וְחוֹזֵר לִתְפִלָּתוֹ, רַשַּׁאי:

en:
חַי m. (Biblical Hebrew; חָיָה)
1) living, alive; living creature; healthy. Berakhot 27ᵇ אלמלא אני חי והוא מת יכול החי וכ׳ if I were alive and he dead, the living one might give the lie to the dead. Ib. V, 5 זה חי this one is destined to live (recover). Shabbat 94ᵃ, and e. החי נושא את עצמו a living being carries itself (the carrying of a living being on the Sabbath is not unlawful). Ib. X, 5 את החי במטה (he who carries) a living person on a couch; and see from—אבר מן החי, see אֵבֶר.—plural חַיִּים, חַיִּין. Pirkei Avot IV, 22 והח׳ לידון and the living are destined to be judged. Shabbat 94ᵃ בין ח׳ ובין שחוטין whether alive or slaughtered; and from—Pirkei Avot Zar. 5ᵇ (reference. to החי, Breishit VI, 19) שחיין ראשי וכ׳ the ends of whose limbs live (exist).

—2) in natural condition, raw (opposed בשול); unmixed (opposed מָזוּג). Sanhedrin 70ᵃ בשר חי raw meat, יין חי unmixed wine. Pirkei Avot Zar. 38ᵃ, and from הנאכל כמות שהוא חי what is eatable in its natural state; and from—Fem. חַיָּה. Chullin 42ᵃ (reference. to Vayikra XI, 2) ח׳ אכול וכ׳ what is in a healthy condition (viable), you may eat, see טְרֵפָה. [V. חַיָּה.]

טָרַף (Biblical Hebrew; compare טָרַד) [to move with vehemence,]
1) to tear, prey. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 26 טוֹרֵף ואוכל tears in order to satisfy his appetite. Kohelet Rabbah to X, 11 הארי ט׳ the lion goes out for prey. Sotah 47ᵇ טוֹרְפֵי טֶרֶף those robbing (the poor). Zevachim 53ᵇ חלקו של טוֹרֵף the territory of the tearer (wolf = Benjamin, Breishit XLIX, 27). Bava Kamma 116ᵇ לטוֹרְפָהּ to plunder it; and from

—2) to cast with force, knock, strike against; to throw away, reject, eject. Chullin III, 3 טְרָפָהּ בכותל he cast or knocked the bird against the wall. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 11; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 2 מגרשה אני טוֹרְפָהּ אני I will divorce her, I will cast her out (compare טָרַד).—Berakhot 5ᵇ טוֹרְפִין לו וכ׳ his prayer is thrown in his face (refused). Yerushalmi Yevamot XVI, 15ᵈ top טְרָפַנִי, see טָרַד.

—3) to seize forcibly. Yoma IV, 1 ט׳ בקלפי he took the ballot out with haste.—Esp. to seize for a debt. Bava Metzia 15ᵃ ובא ב"ח וטְרָפָהּ and a creditor of the previous owner came and seized it, see טִירְפָּא.

—4) to chop, hash, to beat, mix. Shabbat XIX, 2 ט׳ יין ושמן beat wine and oil; and e.—Part. pass. טָרוּף, f. טְרוּפָה. Ib. 38ᵃ בשר ט׳ chopped meat. Pirkei Avot Zar. II, 6, see טָרִית. Yerushalmi Niddah IV, 51ᵃ (of a foetus). Shabbat VIII, 5 (80ᵇ) ביצה ט׳ an egg beaten and mixed with oil; and from V. טָרוּף.

—5) to hackle, comb (flax or wool). Kilayim IX, 1. Yerushalmi Orlah III, 63ᵃ; Yerushalmi Ketubot VI, end, 31ᵃ צמר בכור שטְרָפוֹ wool of a first-born that has been hackled (and mixed up with, other wool).

—6) to scrape, scour, to plane. Makhshirin II, 4 הטוֹרֵף את גגו (Variant המטהר) if one scrubs his roof; Tosefta ib. I, 8.

—7) to make טְרֵפָה, to inflict an organic defect. Chullin 85ᵇ, sq. צא טְרוֹף go and maim the animal (before slaughtering it).

Nifal - נִטְרַף
1) to become t’refah. Ib. 9ᵃ, and e. במה נִטְרְפָה from what cause it became t’refah

—2) to be in disorder, a) (with דעה, or לב) to be confused, bewildered, not fully conscious. Yerushalmi Shabbat II, 5ᵇ bottom of page נִטְרְפָה דעתו של אבא my father’s mind is unclear; Sanhedrin 68ᵃ. Ib. 43ᵃ כדי שתִּטָּרֵף דעתו (not שתטרוף) that his (the culprit’s) consciousness may be benumbed; Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 10.—Ib. נ׳ לבו his mind becomes confused (from drinking); and from—b) (with שעה, of political disturbances) to be troubled. Sanhedrin 11ᵃ; Sotah 48ᵇ; Tosefta ib. XIII, 5 נטרפה (ה)שעה the political condition was too much troubled (persecutions prevailing). Yerushalmi Demai V, 24ᵈ bottom of page; and e.

Piël - טֵרֵף
1) to shake vehemently, constantly. Sukkah III, 9 כל העם מטָרְפִין בלולביהן ed. Yerushalmi (Mishnah ed. Pesachim מט׳את לול׳; ed. מנעועין) all the people shook their branches constantly (during the recitation at Hallel, contradistinguished to נענע).

—2) to unbalance (the mind, compare טִלְטֵל).—Part. pass. מְטוֹרָף. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 10 לבו מ׳ וכ׳ his mind is disturbed and he talks improper things, see supra.

—3) to reject one’s petition, to refuse. Part. pass. מְטוֹרָף. Berakhot V, 5 שהוא מ׳ that he (the patient for whom prayer is said) is rejected (bound to die), opposed מקובל accepted.

—4) to disfigure, to make ungainly by spots, incisions &c., see טָרוּף). Part. pass. as ab. Kohelet Rabbah to X, 11 the serpent is asked מפני מה גופך מט׳ why has thy body been disfigured (see Breishit III, 14)?

—5) to cast about (a ship on high sea), see Hithpaël—Part. pass. as ab.; pl. מְטוֹרָפִים, מְטוֹרָפִין. Yevamot 47ᵃ, see סָחַף.

Hifil - הִטְרִיף
1) to become t’refah, to be afflicted with a fatal organic disease. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 12, end; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to VI, 4; Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Vayhi p. 10ᵃ, and e. לא הִטְרִיפוּ the animals were found to be free from an organic disease.—[
2) (in later liter.) to declare t’refah.]

—3) (denominative of טֶרֶף) a) to cover with foliage. Yalkut Breishit 119, see רָטַב.—b) to sprout with moisture, be sappy. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 69 ה׳ מצות וכ׳ (Yalkut Judges 38 הפריח) sprouted with good deeds &c., see רָטַב.—[
4) to distribute food, see טָרָף.]

Hithpaël - הִיטָּרֵף, , Nithpa. נִיטָּרֵף to be tossed about, to be in a storm near the shore. Taanit III, 7 (19ᵃ) על הספינה המִיטָּרֶפֶת וכ׳ for a ship which is seen from the coast to be tossed about; Taanit 14ᵃ המְטוֹרֶפֶת (see supra; Arukh ed. Kohelet נִטְרֶפֶת Nif.). Tosefta Shabbat XIII (XIV), 11 נִיטָּרְפָה ספינה וכ׳ the ship has been thrown back several times (was prevented from landing by the breakers).

כְּמוֹת (= כְּמוֹ את, compare כְּוָת) like, as. Yerushalmi Ma'aser Sheni IV, 54ᵈ כ׳ שהוא מוכר according to the selling price. Shabbat 51ᵃ, and from כ׳ שהוא (חי) in its natural condition (raw). Ketubot 17ᵃ כלה כ׳ שהיא the bride at weddings must be praised according to her perfections (without exaggeration); and from—With suffixes: כְּמוֹתִי, כְּמוֹתְךָ &c. like myself, like thyself &c. Bava Metzia 59ᵇ אם הלכה כ׳ if the law is in accordance with my opinion, see כְּוָת. Yerushalmi Nedarim I, 36ᵈ bottom of page כ׳ ירבו וכ׳ may there be many like thee &c.; (Bavli ib. 9ᵇ כָּמוֹךָ). Berakhot V, 5, and from שלוחו של אדם כְּמוֹתוֹ a man’s messenger is like himself, i.e. action by proxy is legal; and from

צִיבּוּר, צִבּ׳ m. (Biblical Hebrew צִבֻּר; צָבַר)
1) heap, pile. Pesachim 10ᵃ צ׳ אחד של חמץ one pile of leavened matter.—plural צִיבּוּרִים, צִיבּוּרִין, צִבּ׳. Ib. 9ᵇ. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 39 עשה צ׳ וכ׳ he put up piles of sand and brought sieves &c.; Yalkut ib. 62, end; Yalkut Nehemiah 1071, see צֶבֶר. Bava Metzia II, 2 צִבּוּרֵי פירות fruit in piles; צ׳ מעות coins in piles. Yerushalmi Peah VI, 19ᶜ bottom of page (reference. to ציבורי זיתים, ib. VI, 5) מה בין הצ׳ מה בין הזיתים what difference is there whether there are piles of olives or olives (not piled up)?; and from

—2) congregation, community. Berakhot V, 5 ואם שליח צ׳ הוא and if it happened to him as a deputy of the congregation (public reader of prayers). Rosh Hashanah 18ᵃ גזר דין של צ׳ an evil decree concerning a community, opposed יחיד. Pirkei Avot II, 2, see עָמֵל. Sotah 40ᵃ אימת צ׳ the fear (respect) of the assembled congregation. Berakhot 8ᵃ בשעה שהצ׳ מתפללין when the congregation is in prayer. Zevachim V, 3 חטאת הצ׳ communal sin-offerings; and from

קָבַל I (Biblical Hebrew; compare חבל and חבר) [to seize; to join, meet, correspond.]

Piël - קִבֵּל to receive, accept; to take an obligation upon one’s self; to contract, agree. Zevachim II, 1 כל הזבחים שק׳ דמן זר וכ׳ all sacrifices whose blood was received (in a vessel) by a non-priest &c. Ib. 4 ק׳ והלך וזרק וכ׳ if he received the blood, or carried or sprinkled it with the thought of disposal at an unlawful time. Ib. 3; and from—Pirkei Avot I, 1 משה ק׳ וכ׳ Moses received the (traditional) law from Sinai, and handed it over to &c. Ib. 4 קִבְּלוּ מהם (Variant ממנו) received the traditions from them. Ib. 3 לקַבֵּל וכ׳, see עֶבֶד. Eruvin 72ᵇ מְקַבְּלֵי פרס; ib. 73ᵃ מְקַבְּלוֹת, see פְּרָס. Pirkei Avot I, 15 הוי מְקַבֵּל את כל וכ׳ receive every man &c., see סֵבֶר. Ketubot 58ᵃ (a mnemonical formula) ק׳ מסר והלך if he (the betrothed) accepted (was satisfied to marry her in spite of blemishes discovered), or if the father handed his daughter over to the groom’s delegates, or if the father (or his delegates) went along with the groom’s delegates; Kiddushin 11ᵃ. Ketubot 56ᵇ, and from ק׳ עליו אחריות if he assumed the guaranty. Demai II, 2, sq. המקבל עליו וכ׳ he that obligates himself &c., see נֶאֱמָן. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 3 והם לא קבלו על וכ׳ and did they not receive (punishment) for what they did? Ib. אינו מקבל מוסר does not accept correction. Menachot 96ᵇ, and from מקבל טומאה susceptible of levitical uncleanness; and see from—Esp. to take on lease, to rent a field either on shares (see אָרִיס) or at a fixed rent (see חָכִיר). Bava Metzia IX, 1. Ib. 9 קִבְּלָהּ הימנו לשבע וכ׳ if he rented it of him for seven years. Ib. 10 קבלה הימנו שבע … בשבע וכ׳ if he rented it for ‘seven years at a rent of seven hundred Zuz’, the Sabbatical year is not included; and from—ק׳ פנים, see Hifil—ק׳ קיבולת, see קִיבּוֹלֶת.—Part. pass. מְקוּבָּל a) accepted, acceptable, well-liked, beloved. Berakhot V, 5, see טָרַף. Ib. 17ᵃ ויהא מק׳ על הבריות and that he may be well-liked of men.—b) holding a tradition. Peah II, 6 מק׳ אני מר׳ … שקבל וכ׳ I hold a tradition from R. M. who received it of &c.; Nazir 56ᵇ כך מְקוּבְּלַנִי וכ׳; and e.

Hifil - הִקְבִּיל (with פנים or subaudi פנים; interch. with Piël) to ask for a favorable reception, to visit, pay one’s respects to. Yerushalmi Eruvin V, beginning 22ᵇ אילולא דייו אלא שהיה מקבל פני רבו שכל המַקְבִּיל פני רבו כאילו מקבל וכ׳ (not דיין; = אילו לא עשה כלום אלא … דייו) had he done nothing (during the thirteen years of his waiting on his master) but greet his teacher, it were sufficient; for he that pays his respects to his teacher is considered as one waiting on the Divine Presence; Yerushalmi Sanhedrin XI, 30ᵇ top. Chagigah 5ᵇ אתם הִקְבַּלְתֶּם … תזכו להַקְבִּיל וכ׳ you have greeted a countenance that is seen but cannot see (a blind man), may you be permitted to greet the Countenance that sees and cannot be seen. Sanhedrin 42ᵃ אילמלא … להַקְבִּיל פני וכ׳ if Israelites were permitted to greet their Father in heaven only once a month &c.; כל המברך … כאילו מקבל וכ׳ saying the blessing over the new moon in its due time, is, as it were, greeting the Divine Presence; Yalkut Shemot 189 מקביל. Yerushalmi Chagigah I, beginning 75ᵈ והִקְבּילוּ ר׳ י׳ בבקיעין and waited upon (visited) R. J. in B’ḳiin; Yerushalmi Sotah III, 18ᵈ bottom of page; Tosefta Sotah VII, 9, והקבילו פני וכ׳; Chagigah 3ᵃ הלכו להקביל פני וכ׳; and from—Shabbat 152ᵃ, see infra.

Hof. - הוּקְבַּל (with פנים, or ל־) to be placed opposite, be admitted to the presence of, (a polite expression for:) to be visited. Shabbat 152ᵃ מפני מה לא הוּקְבַּלְנוּ פניך … שהוּקְבְּלוּ אבותי לאבותיך early eds. (Manuscript Munich לא הוקבלו, incorr.; later eds. הִקְבַּלְנוּ … שהִקְבִּילוּ Hifil; see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) why were we not permitted to see you on the festive day, as my ancestors used to receive thy ancestors?

Hithpaël - הִתְקַבֵּל,

Nithpaël - נִתְקַבֵּל
1) to be received, accepted. Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., Chaldaic IV, Parah 4 הדם הדם שנ׳ בכלי ‘they shall sprinkle the blood’ (Vayikra I, 5), the blood which has been received in a vessel. Zevachim 34ᵇ, sq.; and e.—Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 44 ספק מִתְקַבֵּל ספק אינו מתקבל it is doubtful, will he or will he not be favorably received. Pirkei Avot d’R. N. Chaldaic IV תפלתו מִתְקַבֶּלֶת ברצון his prayer was accepted with favor; and from

—2) to make one’s self the recipient of, to receive, accept. Ketubot V, 1 הִתְקַבַּלְתִּי ממך וכ׳ I have received at thy hands (on account) one hundred &c. Gittin VI, 1 הִתְקַבֵּל גט זה וכ׳ make thyself the receiver of this letter of divorce in behalf of my wife. Ib. התקבל לי גטי accept my letter of divorce in my behalf; and from

שָׁגַר (Shaf. of גרר; compare נגר) to run, flow.—Part. pass. שָׁגוּר; f. שְׁגוּרָה fluent, spoken without hesitation. Berakhot V, 5 אם ש׳ תפלתי וכ׳ if my prayer is fluent in my mouth, I know &c., see טָרַף; Tosefta ib. III, 3 שָׁגְרָה ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant שגורה).—[Shir HaShirim Rabbah to I, 15 שוגרת, see infra.]

Piël - שִׁיגֵּר
1) to speak with fluency. Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 9 כיון ששִׁיגְּרוּ … בפיהם וכ׳ when they recited (these verses) the whole night with fluency, they considered it a good sign &c.

—2) to make run, to send. Midrash Tanḥuma Mick. 8 תפוש … ושַׁגֵּר אותם לפני arrest them and send them up before me; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 91. Ib. וש׳ בשבילם וכ׳ and sent (messengers) out for them to hunt them up &c. Tosefta Shabbat XIII (XIV), 9 ולהיפרכוס שלהן ש׳ לו וכ׳ and to their commander he sent a present of fifty denars. Berakhot 51ᵃ, sq. מְשַׁגְּרוֹ לאנשי וכ׳ he sends it as a gift to his household. Sanhedrin 59ᵇ אחד משגרו וכ׳ he sent out one (serpent) to the south &c. Bava Batra 146ᵃ. Sotah 35ᵇ שִׁגְּרוּ וכ׳, see נוֹטָרִין and from—Part. pass. מְשׁוּגָּר; f. מְשׁוּגֶּרֶת. Shir HaShirim Rabbah to IV, 1, see רוֹגְלִית; ib. to I, 15 שוגרת correct accordingly).

Hifil - הִשְׁגִּיר [to speak fluently,] to improvise a prayer, change the established form. Yerushalmi Berakhot V, 9ᶜ שליח צבור שה׳ שתים וכ׳ if a reader improvises two or three sections (of the Prayer of Benedictions), we do not make him go back and recite the established form.

שָׁלִיחַ m. (שָׁלַח) deputy, agent. Gittin IV, 1. Ib. 62ᵇ ש׳ להולכה, ש׳ לקבלה, see הוֹלָכָה. Kiddushin 41ᵃ הוא עושה ש׳ he (the husband) can appoint a deputy (to hand to her the letter of divorce); היא עושה ש׳ she can depute an agent (to receive the letter of divorce); הש׳ עושה ש׳ the agent may depute an agent. Ib.ᵇ אין העבד נעשה ש׳ וכ׳ a slave cannot be deputed to receive a letter of divorce. Ib. 42ᵇ, and from אין ש׳ לדבר עבירה there is no deputy for an illegal act, i.e. the responsibility for an illegal act cannot be shifted to the employer. Berakhot V, 5, and e. ש׳ צבור, see צִיבּוּר; and see from—plural שְׁלוּחִים, see שָׁלוּחַ.

שָׁלוּחַ m. (שָׁלַח)
1) messenger, agent, deputy. Kiddushin II, 1 האיש … ובשְׁלוּחוֹ; האשה … ובשְׁלוּחָהּ, see קָדַשׁ. Berakhot V, 5, and from שלוחו של וכ׳, see כְּמוֹת; and from—plural שְׁלוּחִים, שְׁלוּחִין. Rosh Hashanah I, 3, sq. הש׳ יוצאין the messengers went out (to announce the New Moon). Sukkah 10ᵇ; 26ᵃ אנן שְׁלוּחֵי מצוה אנן we are out on a religious message. comments.en: Rebbi Yehudah says, “If a person is fluent with his prayer it is a good sign for him, and if he is not fluent with his prayer it is a bad sign for him.”
comments.he: ר' יהודה אומר אם שגורה תפלתו בפיו סימן יפה הוא לו ואם לאו סימן רע הוא לו.

המתפלל תפלת המוספין בין משקרב תמיד של שחר בין עד שלא קרב תמיד של שחר יצא. ר' עקיבא או' אם שגורה תפלתו בפיו סימן יפה לו, ואם לאו סימן רע לו. הוא היה או' כל שרוח הבריות נוחה ממנו רוח המקום נוחה ממנו. כל שאין רוח הבריות נוחה ממנו אין רוח המקום נוחה ממנו. כל שרוח עצמו נוחה בשלו סימן יפה לו, אין רוח עצמו נוחה בשלו סימן רע לו.

שמנה משמרות תיקן משה לכהונה, ושמנה ללוייה. משעמד דוד ושמואל הרואה, עשאום עשרים וארבע משמרות כהונה ועשרים וארבע משמרות לויה, שנ' המה יסד דוד ושמואל הרואה באמונתם, אילו משמרות כהונה ולויה. עמדו נביאים שבירושלם וקבעו שם עשרים וארבעה עמודים, כנגד עשרים וארבע משמרות כהונה ולויה, שנ' צו את בני ישראל ואמרת אליהם את קרבני לחמי, אי איפשר לומ' כל ישראל, אלא מלמד ששלוחו של אדם כמותו.

comments.en: Just like the Torah established a set time to read the Shema, so too the Sages established a set time for [the] prayer [of Shemoneh Esreh]. Why did they say [that] the morning prayer [of Shmoneh Esreh can be prayed only] until noon? Because the morning Tamid (daily offering) [sacrifice] could be brought [only] until noon. Rebbi Yehudah says, “[The morning prayer of Shmoneh Esreh can be prayed only] until [the end of the first] four hours [of the day].” And why did they say that the Mincha (afternoon) prayer [of Shemoneh Esreh can only be prayed] until the evening? Because the afternoon Tamid [sacrifice] could be brought [only] until the evening. Rebbi Yehudah says, “[The Mincha prayer of Shmoneh Esreh can be prayed only] until Plag Hamincha.” And when is Plag Hamincha? Eleven minus one quarter hours [of the day] (i.e. 10 ¾ hours). And why did they say that the evening prayer [of Shmoneh Esreh] does not have a set time? Because the limbs and fats [of the sacrifices] could be brought the whole night. And why did they say that the Mussaf prayer [of Shmoneh Esreh can be prayed] the whole day? Because the Mussaf (additional offering) sacrifice could be brought the whole day. Rebbi Yehudah says, “[The Mussaf prayer can be prayed] until [the end of the first] seven hours [of the day].”
comments.he: כשם שנתנה תורה קבע לקרות שמע כך נתנו חכמים קבע לתפלה מפני מה אמרו תפלת השחר עד חצות שכן תמיד של שחר [היה] קרב עד חצות רבי יהודה אומר עד ד' שעות שכן תמיד של שחר קרב והולך עד ד' שעות ומפני מה אמרו תפלת מנחה עד הערב שכן תמיד של בין הערבים [היה] קרב עד הערב ר' יהודה אומר עד פלג המנחה שהרי תמיד של בין הערבים קרב והולך עד פלג המנחה ומפני מה אמרו תפלת הערב אין לה קבע שהרי אברין ופדרין קרבין והולכין כל הלילה ומפני מה אמרו תפלת מוספין כל היום שהרי קרבן מוספין קרב והולך כל היום רבי יהודה אומר עד שבע שעות שהרי קרבן של מוסף קרב והולך עד שבע שעות.

שמונה משמרות תקן משה לכהונה ושמונה ללוים משעמד דוד ושמואל הרואה עשאום כ"ד משמרות כהונה וכ"ד משמרות [לויה] שנאמר (דברי הימים א ט׳:כ״ב) המה יסד דוד ושמואל הרואה באמונתם אלו משמרות כהונה ולויה עמדו נביאים שבירושלים וקבעו שם כ"ד מעמדות כנגד כ"ד משמרות כהונה ולויה שנאמר (במדבר כ״ח:ב׳) צו את בני ישראל ואמרת אליהם את קרבני לחמי אי אפשר לומר כל ישראל אלא מלמד ששלוחו של אדם כמותו.

comments.en: But one is gone from me, and I said: Alas, he was torn by a beast! And I have not seen him since.
comments.he: וַיֵּצֵ֤א הָֽאֶחָד֙ מֵֽאִתִּ֔י וָאֹמַ֕ר אַ֖ךְ טָרֹ֣ף טֹרָ֑ף וְלֹ֥א רְאִיתִ֖יו עַד־הֵֽנָּה׃

sections.en: Concluding its discussion of the halakhot of prayer, the mishna discusses less practical aspects of prayer. One who prays and realizes that he erred in his prayer, it is a bad omen for him; it indicates to him that his prayer was not accepted. And if he who erred is the communal prayer leader, it is a bad omen for those who sent him, because a person’s agent has legal status equivalent to his own. On a similar note, they said about Rabbi Ḥanina ben Dosa that he would pray on behalf of the sick and immediately after his prayer he would say: This one shall recover from his illness and live and this one shall die. When they said to him: From where do you know? He said to them: If my prayer is fluent in my mouth as I recite it and there are no errors, I know that my prayer is accepted. And if not, I know that my prayer is rejected.
sections.he: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל וְטָעָה, סִימָן רַע לוֹ. וְאִם שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר הוּא, סִימָן רַע לְשׁוֹלְחָיו, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁשְּׁלוּחוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם כְּמוֹתוֹ. אָמְרוּ עָלָיו עַל רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶן דּוֹסָא, כְּשֶׁהָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל עַל הַחוֹלִים וְאוֹמֵר, זֶה חַי וְזֶה מֵת. אָמְרוּ לוֹ, מִנַּיִן אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ. אָמַר לָהֶם, אִם שְׁגוּרָה תְפִלָּתִי בְּפִי, יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁהוּא מְקֻבָּל. וְאִם לָאו, יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי שֶׁהוּא מְטֹרָף:
